## Body

#254 merged as 2f269126 and was proven live 2026-11-19. Supersedes notes 0a651ab and 50db165.
- Copilot `/restart` respawns the CLI under the old process: the old pid stays alive as the loader (the parent of the new pid), and the registry moves to the new pid and proc_start. Seat id, session and spawn_id don't change. So "is the old pid gone?" is the wrong check. Check that registry.proc changed and that the old pid is the new one's ppid.
- To live-prove a seat route: spawn with `pij_spawn {harness:copilot, role:worker, layout:window}` (you become its parent), then read the row with `pij-rs --json list | jq '.. | objects | select(.id?=="<seat>")'` (`.data[]` errors). POST with `Authorization: Bearer $(cat ~/.pij-rs/daemon.key)` to 127.0.0.1:7461. Receipts: in the ro sqlite, the `jobs` table (kind `delivery-control:<seat>`) and `spine_events` (not `events`).
- Notices must name runnable commands: the shim's `pij revive` is unported (E-RS-UNPORTED), so use `pij-rs revive`, with the seat quoted by `pij_core::directory::shell_word`. The reviewer blocked round 2 on exactly this.
- Mutation-check a per-key lock: an unshared slot made the concurrent test fail as [Restart, NotRestarted], so the test is not vacuous.
- Open C34 follow-up (not done): after a wall-clock correction plus a daemon restart, the window rebuilt from the spine can look expired early.
